title: Larger-first order in deep ComCat pairs remained clear under a 365-day group sign test in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether larger-first order in 112 deep earthquake pairs depends on seven-day independence groups. We kept the pairs fixed and joined deep events within 200 km and 365 days into broader groups. The larger event came first in 81 pairs (72.3%). The number of occupied groups fell from 48 to 20. The exact two-sided fair-sign probability rose from 0.000352 to 0.01139. The conditional 95% group bootstrap interval widened from 60.2-85.3% to 55.2-88.9%. One broad group held 64 of 112 pairs. A planned 730-day grouping gave p = 0.02245. Thus the order result remained clear under these specified sign assumptions, but support weakened as groups merged. This is an assumption check on the same catalog, not independent confirmation, a dependence-time estimate or proof of triggering. The package includes code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a separate numerical audit and a figure. Source event records stay outside the package.

display.caption: The pair set stays fixed. Longer grouping windows widen conditional share intervals and raise exact fair-sign probabilities. All tests assume independent symmetric group scores.

citations.reason: Prior pair-order result and same source snapshot. We hold its pair set fixed and change independence groups.
Its broad groups motivate this separate grouping sensitivity test. It compared short and long pair windows; we use only the fixed short pairs.
